newsitem.title: USA: FY98 farm spending bill delayed until September.
newsitem.headline: FY98 farm spending bill delayed until September.

text.p: House and Senate negotiators will not meet until September to craft a compromise fiscal 1998 agriculture appropriations bill, a House aide said Monday.

Both chambers approved separate versions of the bill last week. But before work can begin on a compromise package, a number of overarching issues affecting funding for several appropriations bills must be resolved, the aide said.
That won't happen before Congress adjourns for its traditional month-long August recess, the aide said.
The Senate bill provides $50.7 billion for U.S. Agriculture Department and Food and Drug Administration programs compared to the House level of $49.5 billion.
A key difference in the two bills is the funding level for the Export Enhancement Program, which is used to subsidize agricultural exports.
The Senate capped funding at $150 million and the House at $205 million, both of which were well below the Clinton administration request of $500 million.
